threads.thread_goal: Align on current routines, constraints, and select pilot group for the program.

messages.text: Hi team, we're kicking off the Integrated Wellbeing Program for our group home. The goal is to design and pilot a structured program that brings together care, pedagogy, and vocational skills over the next 21 days. We need to start by understanding what's already happening here—current routines, obligations, and where we have flexibility. I'd like to ask: can we map out a full week of current activities for all youths? This will help us identify free time slots and potential conflicts. Also, we should discuss which youths would be good candidates for the first pilot group. Let's aim to have T1 (current routines mapping) started today and shared by end of week. Thoughts?

I can start pulling together the routines data today. I've got notes on most of the youths' weekly commitments—school times, therapy sessions, and what they're already doing in free time. I'll organize it by youth and flag the conflicts I see. Should I include informal activities too, like who hangs out together or what they do on their own?

Yes, absolutely include informal activities—that's actually really important. It shows us what naturally engages them and where we might build from. Once you have that, I'll review it and we can validate together. That will feed into A1.

On the pilot group selection—I think we should be careful about who we include. Some of our youths are dealing with quite a bit right now. Should we prioritize those who are more stable, or do we want a mix? I'm thinking about the trauma-informed angle here.

Good point. I'd suggest we aim for a mix but with clear criteria: youths who can benefit from structure and have at least some capacity to engage, but not necessarily the most 'stable' ones. The program itself is designed to support wellbeing, so we're not excluding people based on need. However, we do need to make sure we're not setting anyone up to fail. Let's look at the routines data first, then we can discuss specific names. We'll need to confirm D1 once we have that picture.

I'm ready to help with the mapping. I can also check our therapy and external appointment calendar to make sure we're not missing anything. Once we know the free slots, we'll have a clearer picture for D2—the time windows for structured activities.

That's helpful. From my side, I'll need to know what times work best so I can plan the vocational modules around them. I'm assuming we'll have some flexibility, but I want to make sure the taster sessions don't clash with school.

Most of the youths are in school until 3 PM on weekdays, and a couple have therapy on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 4 PM. So we've got late afternoons and evenings, plus weekends. I'll have all this in the sheet by tomorrow.

Perfect. So we're looking at 3:30 PM onwards on most weekdays, and more flexibility on weekends. That's actually a decent window. Once we have A1 finalized, we can lock in D2. Let's aim for that by end of this week.
And for the pilot group—should we aim for a specific number? Like 4–6 youths to start, or are we thinking bigger?

I'd suggest starting with 5–7 youths. Small enough to manage closely and gather good feedback, but large enough to see patterns. We can discuss specific names once we have the routines data and understand who's available and interested. Let's make D1 a decision point once we've reviewed A1 together.
I'll have the routines sheet ready by tomorrow EOD. Then we can all review and discuss the pilot group names by Friday?
Sounds good. I'll cross-check the external commitments and add any notes to the sheet. Should be ready by tomorrow as well.
Great. So timeline: A1 finalized by tomorrow EOD, team review Thursday, and we confirm D1 and D2 by Friday. That gives us a solid foundation to move into schedule design next week.
Works for me. I'll start sketching out some vocational module ideas in the meantime so we're ready to integrate them once the schedule is locked.

Quick update: I've got the routines sheet mostly done. A few notes—three youths have pretty packed schedules, but there's still room. Two of them are quite engaged already, so they might be good pilot candidates. I'll upload the full A1 by end of day.
Excellent. That's the kind of detail we need. Once it's up, I'll review and we can start thinking about who fits the pilot group criteria. Looking forward to seeing A1.
I've also confirmed the therapy and appointment slots. No major surprises—just the Tuesday and Thursday sessions we already knew about. I'll add a note to A1 so it's all in one place.

Perfect. So we have a clear picture now. Looking at the data, I'd propose we include youths 2, 4, 5, 6, and 7 in the pilot—they have the flexibility and the engagement potential. Does that align with what you're seeing?
Yes, that makes sense. Those five are a good mix—different needs and interests, but all capable of engaging. I think they'll respond well to the structure.
I agree. And for the time windows—based on A1, we've got 3:30 PM to 6 PM on weekdays, and more flexibility on Saturday afternoons. Does that work for everyone?
That works. I can fit the vocational modules into those slots. Afternoon sessions are actually better for hands-on activities anyway.
Confirmed. 3:30–6 PM weekdays and Saturday afternoons. That's our window. I'll make sure no external appointments clash with those times.

Excellent. So we have D1 confirmed: pilot group is youths 2, 4, 5, 6, 7. And D2 confirmed: structured activities will run 3:30–6 PM weekdays and Saturday afternoons. This is our foundation. Next step is TH2—designing the weekly schedule. I'll draft that and post it early next week.
Great. I'm ready to help with co-designing activities with the youths once we have the schedule framework. That's T6, right?
Yes, exactly. We'll tackle that in TH2. For now, we've got a solid TH1 outcome. Let's move forward.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the weekly structured activity schedule and co-designed activities.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted a first version of the weekly structured activity schedule for our pilot group. It's based on the time windows we confirmed (3:30–6 PM weekdays, Saturday afternoons) and incorporates education support, leisure, and social skills blocks. I've also left space for the vocational modules and at least one co-designed youth activity per week. Can you review A5 and give me feedback? I'm looking for: Does it fit your role? Are there conflicts? What's missing? Let's aim to finalize this by mid-week so we can move into implementation.

I've looked at A5. The structure looks good overall. One thing—I notice Monday and Wednesday are pretty packed with education support. Can we spread that out a bit? Some of the youths get tired if it's too dense. Also, I'm ready to start the co-design conversations with them this week. Should I do that before or after we finalize the schedule?

Good catch on the density. I'll redistribute the education blocks. On the co-design—I'd say start the conversations now, actually. Get their ideas, and we'll weave the best ones into the final schedule. That way they feel heard and invested. That's T6. Can you document what they suggest?

I've reviewed A5. The vocational slots look good—I see Thursday and Saturday are blocked for taster sessions. That works with my plan. I'm thinking 3–4 modules: basic cooking, CV and job search basics, workshop skills, and maybe digital literacy. Does that fit the schedule?
Those modules sound solid. Yes, Thursday and Saturday work. We'll finalize the exact modules in TH4, but this gives us a good direction. Keep that list handy.

I've read through A5. It looks reasonable. I'm a bit concerned about the leisure block on Friday—is that structured or free choice? I want to make sure we're balancing structure with autonomy, especially for youths who need predictability but also need to feel some control.

That's a really good point. Friday leisure should be semi-structured—we offer options (games, art, sports, music) but they choose. I'll clarify that in the updated A5. It's about giving them agency within a safe frame.

I've looked at A5 as well. One thing I want to flag: we need to make sure the schedule accounts for individual support time. Some of the youths in the pilot group need one-on-one check-ins. Can we build that in, or is that separate from the structured activities?

Good question. Individual support time is separate—that's part of the daily routine and the support plans (A2, which we'll finalize in TH3). The structured activities are group-based, but we can build in flexibility for youths who need to step out for one-on-one time. I'll add a note to A5 about that.

I've started the co-design conversations. The youths have some great ideas—they want a cooking activity, a games night, and one group mentioned wanting to learn about music production. I'll document all of this and share it by tomorrow. Should I ask them to prioritize, or just collect everything?

Collect everything first, then we'll narrow down together. The cooking activity is definitely doable. Music production might need some resources—let's see. Games night is easy. I'll review your notes and we can pick the top two or three for the pilot. That's D4.

Those are good ideas. Cooking is practical and builds life skills. Games night is low-barrier and fun. Music production is interesting but might be complex for a first pilot. I'd lean toward cooking and games night as the two co-designed activities.
I'll document the cooking and games night ideas in detail. I can also ask the youths what they'd want to cook and what games they prefer. That way they feel really involved in the planning.

Perfect. That's exactly the right approach. So here's where we are: I'm updating A5 with the feedback (spreading education blocks, clarifying leisure as semi-structured, adding flexibility for individual support). Once that's done, we can confirm D3. And we'll confirm D4 once we have the detailed co-design notes from you.
Sounds good. I'll finalize my module descriptions in the meantime so we're ready for TH4. Should I be thinking about how to adapt the modules for different ability levels?
Yes, absolutely. That's part of T5. Each module should have options or scaffolding so everyone can participate at their level. We'll discuss that more in TH4, but start thinking about it now.
I'm ready to help integrate the co-designed activities into the final schedule once we confirm them. Just let me know the details.
I'll have the co-design documentation ready by EOD tomorrow. Then we can lock in D4 and finalize A5.
Great. So timeline: updated A5 by tomorrow, co-design notes by tomorrow EOD, then we confirm D3 and D4 by Wednesday. That gives us a solid schedule to launch with by the end of the week.
Works for me. I'm also thinking about how we'll communicate the schedule to the youths—should we present it as final, or invite them to a launch meeting where we explain the reasoning?

Good thinking. I'd suggest a brief launch meeting—maybe 20 minutes—where we explain the structure, highlight the co-designed activities so they see their input, and invite questions. That builds buy-in. We can do that Friday afternoon once A5 is finalized.
I'll help facilitate that. The youths will appreciate seeing their ideas reflected in the schedule.

Perfect. So TH2 outcome: D3 confirmed (weekly schedule approved), D4 confirmed (cooking and games night as co-designed activities), A5 finalized, and youths briefed by Friday. Next is TH3—templates and tools.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on templates and tools: individual plans, handover checklist, and monitoring log.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted three key templates that we'll use throughout the pilot: A2 (Individual Support and Development Plan template), A4 (Shift Handover and Coordination Checklist), and A7 (Wellbeing and Engagement Monitoring Log). These are designed to be simple and practical—something every shift can use consistently without adding huge admin burden. Can you review each one and give me feedback? I'm looking for: Is it clear? Is it usable? What's missing? Let's aim to finalize by end of week so we can train staff and start using them from day one of the pilot.

I've looked at all three. A2 is good—it covers the key areas. One thing: can we add a section for 'youth voice'? Like, what does the youth want to work on? I think that's important for buy-in. A4 looks practical. A7 is simple, which I like, but I want to make sure we're capturing enough to see trends without overwhelming people.

Excellent point on youth voice in A2. I'll add that section—'Youth's own goals and priorities.' That's actually core to trauma-informed practice. On A7, what specific trends are you thinking about? Participation? Mood? Conflicts?
I'd say participation, mood, and engagement in activities. Maybe also note any incidents or concerns. That way we can see if the program is helping or if we need to adjust for specific youths.

I agree. And for A4, the handover checklist—I want to make sure we're capturing continuity. Like, if a youth had a difficult moment in the morning, the afternoon shift needs to know. Can we add a section for 'carry-over concerns'?
Yes, absolutely. That's critical for consistency. I'll add 'Carry-over concerns and follow-up actions' to A4. That way nothing falls through the cracks between shifts.

I've reviewed the templates. A2 looks solid once the youth voice section is added. A4 is clear. For A7, I'm wondering if we should also track attendance at vocational sessions separately, or is that part of the general participation metric?

Good question. I think vocational attendance can be part of the general participation metric in A7, but we can also track it separately in the vocational module records (A6). That way you have detail for your sessions, and we have the overview in A7.
That makes sense. So A7 is the high-level overview, and each activity area (vocational, education, etc.) has its own detail. I can work with that.

Exactly. So here's what I'm updating: A2 gets a 'Youth voice' section. A4 gets 'Carry-over concerns.' A7 will track participation, mood, engagement, and incidents. All three will be simple enough for any shift to use. I'll have revised versions by tomorrow. Then we can confirm D5 and D6.

One more thing—for A2, should we include a section on trauma history or triggers? I want to make sure we're not asking staff to diagnose, but knowing what we know about each youth's background could help with the support plan.

That's important. I'll add a section called 'Known sensitivities and strengths'—not a diagnosis, but things like 'loud noises can be triggering' or 'responds well to one-on-one time.' That's practical and trauma-informed without overstepping.
Perfect. That's the right balance. I'm satisfied with the direction of all three templates now.
Agreed. These templates are going to make a real difference in how we support the youths. I'm ready to start using them once they're finalized.
Same here. These will help me track how youths are progressing in the vocational modules too.

Great. So I'll have the revised A2, A4, and A7 ready by tomorrow EOD. Then we can do a final review and confirm D5 (A2 approved) and D6 (A4 and A7 approved) by Wednesday. After that, we'll brief the team on how to use them—that's part of T10.
I can help with the briefing. I'll prepare some talking points on how to use A4 and A7 during handovers.
Perfect. That would be really helpful. We'll coordinate the briefing schedule once the templates are locked. TH3 is shaping up well.
I'm also thinking about how we'll introduce A2 to the youths. Should they see their own plans, or is that just for staff?

Good question. I'd say yes, they should see their own plans—especially the 'Youth voice' section. We can present it as 'Here's what we're working on together' rather than 'Here's what we think you need.' That's empowering and transparent.
I like that approach. It's collaborative and respectful. Aligns with the whole philosophy of the program.
Exactly. So TH3 outcome: D5 and D6 confirmed, templates finalized, and we're ready to brief staff and introduce the tools to youths. That sets us up for a strong launch.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate vocational skills taster modules within the weekly schedule.

messages.text: Hi team, I've finalized the vocational skills taster module plan. I'm proposing four modules: basic cooking (life skills and confidence), CV and job search basics (future planning), workshop skills (hands-on, practical), and digital literacy (modern skills). Each module is 4–5 sessions, adapted for different ability levels. I've drafted A6 with objectives, materials, and timing. The modules fit into the Thursday and Saturday slots we confirmed. Can you review and let me know: Do these modules make sense? Are there any conflicts with the schedule? What adjustments do you need? Let's finalize by mid-week so we can start the first sessions next week.

This looks really solid. The four modules cover a good range—practical life skills, future planning, hands-on work, and digital. I like that you've thought about ability levels. One question: how are you planning to handle youths who might be anxious about trying something new? Any scaffolding or buddy system?

Good point. I'm thinking of pairing youths who are more confident with those who are hesitant, at least for the first session. And I'll make sure the first activity in each module is low-pressure—like, for cooking, we start with something simple they can succeed at. That builds confidence.
I like that approach. The buddy system is good for engagement and peer support. I can help facilitate that—maybe I'll be in the cooking sessions to help manage the group dynamics.
That would be really helpful. Having another adult in the room, especially for cooking, is important for safety and support. Can you be there for the Thursday sessions?
Yes, I can do Thursday. For Saturday, I'd need to check the rota, but I'll make it work if possible.

I've reviewed A6. The modules are well-structured. One thing I'm thinking about: how do we handle youths who might not be interested in a particular module? Is attendance mandatory, or can they opt out?

That's a good question. I'd say the modules are part of the structured program, so attendance is expected, but we can offer choice within that. Like, 'You're doing a vocational module this week—which one interests you?' That respects autonomy while maintaining structure.

I like that. So they choose which module, but they're expected to participate in one. That works with my plan. I can offer the modules in a rotation so everyone gets exposure to all four over the pilot period.
That's a good structure. And for the schedule—Thursday 3:30–5 PM and Saturday 2–4 PM, right? I want to make sure there are no conflicts with external appointments.
Yes, those times work for me. And I've checked—no therapy sessions or school commitments at those times for the pilot group.
Perfect. So we have D7 and D8 shaping up: D7 is confirming the four modules (cooking, CV, workshop, digital), and D8 is confirming Thursday 3:30–5 PM and Saturday 2–4 PM. Does everyone agree?
Yes, I'm good with that. The modules are solid and the times work.
Agreed. I think this is a strong vocational component for the pilot.
Confirmed. No conflicts. We're good to go.

Great. So I'll finalize A6 with the rotation schedule and any last tweaks. I'll also prepare a brief intro for the youths—explaining what each module is about and why it matters. Should I do that at the launch meeting?

Yes, that's perfect. At the Friday launch meeting, you can give a quick overview of the vocational modules. Keep it short and exciting—'Here's what you'll learn and why it matters for your future.' That builds interest.
I'll help with the launch meeting too. We can make it interactive—maybe let them ask questions about the modules.

Excellent. So TH4 outcome: D7 and D8 confirmed, A6 finalized, and we're ready to launch the vocational modules next week. The youths will be briefed at the Friday meeting. After that, we move into T9—running the actual sessions and gathering feedback.

threads.thread_goal: Review first two weeks of pilot, discuss incidents, and agree on adjustments.

messages.text: Hi team, we've completed the first two weeks of the pilot. Overall, it's going well, but we've learned some things. I've compiled A8—a summary of feedback from youths and staff, key themes, and proposed adjustments. The main points: youths are engaging well with the structured activities, the co-designed cooking and games nights are hits, but we've had a couple of incidents that required de-escalation. The handover checklist (A4) has been really helpful for continuity. The monitoring log (A7) shows mostly positive trends, but two youths are still hesitant about the vocational modules. Let me know your thoughts on the feedback and what adjustments you'd recommend. We need to decide: Do we keep the current pilot group (D1 revisited), or make changes? And which co-designed activities are working best (D4 revisited)?

I've read A8. The feedback is really positive overall. The youths are definitely more engaged than before the program started. On the two who are hesitant about vocational modules—I think it's just nerves. They're watching others do it and getting interested. I'd give them another week or two before we make any changes. I don't think we need to adjust the pilot group.

I agree. The hesitant youths are watching the others and asking questions. I think they'll join in soon. No need to change the group. On the vocational side, the cooking module has been the most popular so far. The CV module is a bit abstract for some of them, but I'm working on making it more concrete—like, 'Here's what you're good at' rather than 'Here's how to write a CV.'

That's a good adjustment. Making it personal and concrete is more engaging. So on D1, it sounds like we're keeping the current pilot group. And on D4, cooking is definitely a keeper. Games night is also working well. Should we keep both, or rotate in something else?

I'd keep both cooking and games night. They're low-barrier, fun, and the youths are really engaged. The music production idea that came up earlier—maybe we could introduce that as a third activity in week three? See if there's interest?
I like that idea. We could do a simple music activity—like, creating a playlist together or learning about different genres. Nothing too complex, but it taps into their interest.

That could work. Let's keep cooking and games night as the core co-designed activities, and we can pilot the music activity in week three. If it works, we keep it. If not, we adjust. That's responsive to what the youths are telling us.

I've been tracking the monitoring data in A7. The trends are positive—participation is up, mood is generally stable, and we've had only two incidents in two weeks, which is actually good. The handover checklist has made a real difference in continuity. Staff are using it consistently.
That's really encouraging. The tools are working. On the two incidents—were they handled well? Did the crisis guideline (A3) help?

Yes, both were handled well. Staff used the de-escalation steps from A3, and both youths calmed down quickly. One incident was a conflict between two youths during games night—we separated them, gave them space, and they reconnected later. The other was a youth getting overwhelmed during the cooking activity—we let them step out, and they came back when ready. Both situations showed that the structure and the tools are helping.

That's exactly what we want to see—staff responding calmly and the youths recovering. The program is creating a safe enough space for them to try things and work through challenges. That's the whole point.
Absolutely. And the youths are talking about the activities—they're looking forward to them. That's engagement. I think we're on the right track.

Great. So here's what I'm hearing: D1 confirmed—keep the current pilot group. D4 confirmed—keep cooking and games night, pilot music activity in week three. A8 shows positive trends overall. The tools are working. Now, what adjustments do we need to make for weeks three and four? Any tweaks to the schedule or activities?

For the vocational modules, I'd like to adjust the CV module to be more concrete, like I mentioned. And maybe add a reflection activity at the end of each module—'What did you learn? What was hard? What was fun?' That helps consolidate learning and gives us feedback for T9.
Good idea. That reflection piece is important for learning and for gathering feedback. I'll note that in T12—adjustments based on pilot feedback. Can you document those reflections as you go?
Yes, I'll keep notes on the reflections and any adjustments I make. That will feed into the final feedback summary.
For the schedule, I think we're good. The time slots are working. One small thing—can we add a 10-minute buffer between activities for transitions? Some youths need a bit of time to shift gears.
That's a good practical adjustment. I'll update A5 to include transition time. That's part of T12—adjustments based on feedback.

I'd also suggest we do a quick check-in with the youths about what's working and what they'd like to change. We could do that informally or in a group discussion. That keeps them involved in the process.

Excellent idea. That's part of T11—gathering feedback. Can you facilitate a quick group discussion with the youths this week? Just ask them: What's working? What would you change? What do you want to do more of?
Yes, I can do that. I'll keep it casual and fun—maybe over snacks. That usually gets them talking.

Perfect. So here's the plan for weeks three and four: adjust the CV module to be more concrete, add reflection activities, introduce the music activity, add transition time to the schedule, and gather youth feedback. I'll update A5 and A6 with these adjustments. That's T12. We'll also continue monitoring with A7 and refining as we go.
This is good progress. The pilot is working, the youths are engaged, and we're being responsive to feedback. That's exactly what we want.
Agreed. And the tools—A2, A4, A7—are making a real difference in how we're supporting the youths and communicating across shifts. That's a win.

Absolutely. So TH5 outcome: D1 reconfirmed (keep pilot group), D4 reconfirmed (cooking and games night, pilot music activity), and we've identified concrete adjustments for weeks three and four. We're on track for a strong finish to the pilot. Let's keep the momentum going.
